findings.title: Blocked email matching is case-sensitive, so blocks are trivially bypassed
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match lookup: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. The value passed in from EmailValidator is the raw email as the user typed it, and User.new_from_params stores the email as entered (no downcasing before validation), so the blocked list entry 'spammer@spamclub.com' will not match a signup for 'Spammer@SpamClub.com'. A blocked spammer can re-register simply by changing letter case. The email should be normalized (e.g. Email.downcase(email).strip) both in should_block? and in a before_validation callback when BlockedEmail records are created; the uniqueness validation on the model should also be made case-insensitive for the same reason.

findings.title: match_count increment is a read-modify-write that loses updates under concurrency
findings.body: should_block? loads the record, does record.match_count += 1, and calls record.save. Two concurrent signups with the same blocked email both read the same match_count and the second save overwrites the first, so the counter under-counts. Additionally this save runs full validations and silently discards the stat if save returns false. Use an atomic update (e.g. BlockedEmail.update_counters(record.id, match_count: 1) plus update_column for last_match_at) to avoid the race and the extra validations.

findings.title: Blank email gets a misleading 'not allowed from that email provider' error when a whitelist is configured
findings.body: ActiveModel::EachValidator runs on nil values by default. When SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist is present and the email is blank, email_in_restriction_setting? evaluates 'nil =~ regexp' (nil, falsy), so the validator adds I18n.t('user.email.not_allowed') — 'is not allowed from that email provider' — on top of the presence validator's 'can't be blank'. Users see a confusing message implying their provider is banned when they simply left the field empty. Return early when value is blank (or add allow_blank: true and let the presence validator handle it).

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the controller prototype and never cleared
findings.body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is passed to Discourse.Controller.extend, which puts a single mutable array instance on the prototype shared by every instance of CreateAccountController (the classic Ember.extend footgun). Any rejected email pushed in createAccount (line 275) persists for the life of the controller and would leak across instances if the controller is ever recreated (e.g. in tests or container teardown), causing unrelated emails to show 'invalid'. Initialize the array in init() (this._super(); this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))) and consider clearing it after a successful account creation.

findings.title: Any email error marks the address as 'invalid' in the UI, including 'already taken'
findings.body: On account creation failure, the code pushes result.values.email into rejectedEmails whenever result.errors.email exists, and emailValidation then shows I18n.t('user.email.invalid') for that address. But errors.email is also present for failures unrelated to validity — most commonly the email already being registered (uniqueness). After one failed submit, a user trying an already-registered email is told the address is 'invalid', which is wrong and confusing. Either check the specific error message, or have the server distinguish blocked/invalid from taken.
